findings.title: Second `downsize` definition replaces the 5-argument one and breaks emoji resizing
findings.body: Ruby keeps only the last definition of a method name. So `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 silently replaces `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145, and the method now takes 3 or 4 arguments. `Jobs::ResizeEmoji#execute` still calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` with 5 arguments (app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14). Every run of that job will now raise ArgumentError, so custom emoji are never downsized. Give the new method its own name (for example `downsize_to(from, to, dimensions, opts)`), or have the controller pass a geometry string through a separate method. Then remove the dead definition at lines 145-147.

findings.title: Hard-coded 10 MB client limit ignores `max_attachment_size_kb`
findings.body: `validateUploadedFile` is called with `type` set to 'image' or 'attachment' (line 158). Before this change it used `max_<type>_size_kb`. Now both types are capped at a fixed 10 MB. Server-side downsizing only applies to images, yet attachments lose their configured limit too. If an admin set `max_attachment_size_kb` above 10 MB, the browser now rejects attachments the server would accept. If it is set below 10 MB, the alert no longer shows the real limit. Keep `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_attachment_size_kb` for attachments and use the 10 MB pre-downsize cap only when `type === 'image'`. The 413 message at line 246 also shows a hard-coded 10 MB. That number is not tied to any setting or web-server config, so users may be told the wrong limit.

findings.title: Does `tempfile.size` see the downsized file after ImageOptim rewrites it?
findings.body: The loop rereads `tempfile.size` after each `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)`. `convert_with` runs `convert` and then `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!(to)` (app/models/optimized_image.rb:160-165). If image_optim swaps in its result by renaming a new file over the path, the open Tempfile descriptor still points at the old, unlinked inode. In that case `tempfile.size` keeps returning the original size. The loop would then always run all 5 lossy passes, and `Upload.create_for` would get a stale size, or stale content if it reads from the descriptor. Have you checked that the size and content seen through `tempfile` change after a pass? Reading `File.size(tempfile.path)` would avoid depending on this.

findings.title: No tests for the new automatic downsizing path
findings.body: The pull request adds a downsizing loop in `create_upload` and changes the `OptimizedImage` resize/downsize API, but adds no specs. A spec that uploads an oversized image, and one covering `Jobs::ResizeEmoji`, would have caught the `downsize` arity break.

contracts.action: Upload controller downsizes oversized images in place before creating the Upload
contracts.before_after: Before: an image over max_image_size_kb was rejected by Upload.create_for. After: up to 5 passes of `convert -resize 80%>` run on the tempfile path, then create_for is called.
contracts.visible_effect: The upload succeeds with a smaller image, or the size error from create_for is published over MessageBus or returned as JSON (uploads_controller.rb:83).
contracts.failure_mode: convert_with returns false on failure and the loop carries on silently. Whether the tempfile's reported size updates after ImageOptim is unverified.
contracts.open_question: Does image_optim replace the file by rename, which would leave the open Tempfile fd on the old inode?

contracts.before_after: Before: downsize(from,to,w,h,opts). After: only downsize(from,to,dimensions,opts) exists.
contracts.failure_mode: Job fails on every run; custom emoji are left at full size.

summary: The pull request should not merge yet. Adding a second `OptimizedImage.downsize` definition replaces the old 5-argument one, so `Jobs::ResizeEmoji` will raise ArgumentError on every run. The client-side size check is now a fixed 10 MB for attachments as well as images, which ignores `max_attachment_size_kb`. It is also unverified whether the downsize loop sees the shrunk file size after ImageOptim rewrites the file. No tests were added.
